subject.title: Gateway auto-injects toolsAllow into isolated agentTurn crons; null patch doesn't clear it; breaks CLI backend

question: How should OpenClaw repair CLI-backed cron jobs that carry flagless regression-window `toolsAllow` without making explicit per-cron restrictions fail open?
rationale: The remaining failure is source-reproducible, but distinguishing stale auto-default caps from intentional restrictions is a security-boundary choice automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Add Narrow Stale-Default Repair
options.body: Add a doctor/operator or tightly scoped cron repair that marks or clears only provably auto-default regression-window `toolsAllow` values while preserving explicit restrictions.

options.title: Broaden Agent Null Clear
options.body: Let agent-facing `toolsAllow: null` bypass creator-surface re-capping, accepting a larger authority change that needs explicit security approval.

options.title: Document Manual Recreate/Clear
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document that affected jobs must be recreated or cleared through a trusted CLI/API path.

recommendation.title: Add Narrow Stale-Default Repair
recommendation.body: Add a doctor/operator or tightly scoped cron repair that marks or clears only provably auto-default regression-window `toolsAllow` values while preserving explicit restrictions.
